title: How to Start an LLC in Pennsylvania: A Step-by-Step Guide
summary: Start your new business seamlessly with this complete guide to forming an LLC in Pennsylvania, including resources, filing costs and deadlines, and more.
body_markdown:
License and tax requirements depend on where and how the LLC operates. Businesses operating in Philadelphia generally need the city's free commercial activity license. A Philadelphia business generally must file a Business Income and Receipts Tax (BIRT) return even if it has no profit. An active Commercial Activity License (CAL) can also carry a BIRT filing obligation, even when the business has no activity. The former $100,000 exemption has been eliminated.


A business located outside Philadelphia may also need to file if it meets the city's economic-nexus threshold—generally $100,000 in Philadelphia gross receipts during any 12-month period. Pittsburgh has activity-specific business license requirements. Check the city's current licensing guidance rather than relying on a generalized description of business privilege or mercantile tax. Also check the county and municipality where the business operates.
